# SPE Round r01 Plan: Ticket Triage Agent

This plan is the r01 prediction. The spec is your prompt: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." Nothing exists yet, so this round builds the agent, the dataset, the grader, and the harness. It then measures four configurations against the numbers below. If you approve this plan, you also approve the defaults in the Disagreements section. Change any default before you approve.

## 0. Context check (no commit)

1. I will confirm `pwd`, `git remote -v`, `git status`, and the current branch. All commits stay local on the current branch. I will not push.
2. I will confirm that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. I will check it by name and never print the value.
3. I will check the current model IDs and per-token prices in the Claude API docs. The cost predictions below assume $1 in and $5 out per million tokens for the Haiku tier, and $3 in and $15 out for the Sonnet tier. If the docs show other prices, the prediction stays as written. The log will record the wrong price as the broken Why.

## 1. Specify

### Logged defaults

Your prompt leaves these open. I chose a default for each one so the round can run.

| ID | Decision | Default | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Ticket data | 60 synthetic tickets that I write: 40 clear, 12 ambiguous, 8 adversarial (prompt injection, non-English, near-empty body) | You |
| D2 | Output labels | `category` (bug, outage, billing, account_access, feature_request, how_to, spam), `priority` (P1 to P4), `team` (engineering, sre, billing, support, product, none), and `reason` (one sentence, not graded in r01) | You |
| D3 | Meaning of "correctly" | Joint accuracy of at least 85%. A ticket counts as correct when the category and team match exactly and the priority is within one level. P1 recall must also be at least 95%. | You |
| D4 | Meaning of "cheaply" | At most $2.00 per 1,000 tickets, computed from logged token usage times the verified list price | You |
| D5 | Stack | Python with the `anthropic` SDK for the agent and the grader. A Workflow script in JS for the eval. | Claude |
| D6 | Round budget | A hard cap of $10 in API spend for trials | You |

There is one known risk. I write both the tickets and the gold labels, and a Claude model will grade close to how I label. That can inflate accuracy. In r02 I propose that you hand-check 10 gold labels or supply real tickets.

### Requirements (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent reads one ticket (subject and body) and returns JSON with category, priority, team, and reason | Decision D2 | `schema_ok` validator |
| R2 | Joint accuracy is at least 85% on the r01 set | User: "correctly", plus D3 | `joint_ok` |
| R3 | P1 recall is at least 95% (8 P1 tickets in the set) | Decision D3 | `p1_recall` |
| R4 | Cost is at most $2.00 per 1,000 tickets | User: "cheaply", plus D4 | `cost_per_1k` from the usage log |
| R5 | 100% of outputs pass the JSON schema | Decision | `schema_ok` |
| R6 | Instructions inside a ticket body do not change the labels | Decision | `inject_hold` on the 8 adversarial tickets |
| R7 | Trials cannot reach gold labels, graders, or predictions | SPE way | Transcript and payload scan, 0 voids expected |
| R8 | Every API call is logged with input tokens, output tokens, and cost | Decision | Logged calls equal made calls |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

C1 is the base. Each other configuration changes exactly one thing from C1.

| Config | What it is | Change from C1 |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Keyword rules with no model | Removes the model. This is the floor. |
| C1 | Haiku tier, zero-shot prompt with label definitions, strict tool schema, temperature 0 | Base |
| C2 | Same as C1 on the Sonnet tier | Model |
| C3 | Same as C1 plus 8 few-shot examples (about 1,600 extra input tokens) | Prompt |

Runs: C0 runs once on 60 tickets. C1, C2, and C3 each run 3 repeats on 60 tickets.

### Predicted numbers

| Metric (grader check) | C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy % (`cat_exact`) | 60 | 88 | 93 | 92 | Clear tickets are easy for any model. The 12 ambiguous tickets separate the configs. |
| Team accuracy % (`team_exact`) | 58 | 88 | 93 | 92 | Team mostly follows category, so it tracks category. |
| Priority exact % (`pri_exact`) | 45 | 70 | 77 | 77 | Priority is subjective, and gold labels for P2 versus P3 are noisy. |
| Joint accuracy % (`joint_ok`) | 45 | 83 | 90 | 87 | About 38 of 40 clear tickets, 6 of 12 ambiguous, and 6 of 8 adversarial are correct for C1. C2 and C3 gain 1 to 2 tickets in each hard group. |
| P1 recall % (`p1_recall`, n=8) | 62.5 | 87.5 | 100 | 87.5 | A small model misses one P1 that is phrased calmly. Few-shot examples do not fix tone. |
| Injection hold % (`inject_hold`, n=8) | 50 | 75 | 87.5 | 87.5 | Rules trigger on injected keywords. The strict schema helps every model. |
| Schema valid % (`schema_ok`) | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | Forced tool use with a strict schema. Rules emit fixed JSON. |
| Cost USD per 1,000 tickets (`cost_per_1k`) | 0.00 | 1.50 | 4.50 | 3.10 | About 1,000 input and 100 output tokens per ticket, at assumed list prices. C3 adds 1,600 input tokens. |
| All bars met (1 = yes) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | C1 meets the cost bar but misses the 85% bar. C2 and C3 meet the accuracy bar but miss the cost bar. |

Headline prediction: no configuration meets both "correctly" and "cheaply" in r01. Round r02 will most likely test prompt caching or a shorter few-shot set on C3.

Naive guess for the log: every model config scores 85% joint, and costs follow price arithmetic alone. The log will say plainly if this guess beats the table.

Verdict rule: a cell matches when the accuracy is within 5 points, the cost is within 25%, and P1 recall is within one ticket.

## 3. Evaluate

### Build (after the predict commit)

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `triage/agent.py` | Calls the API with one ticket and the tool schema. Logs usage. |
| `triage/rules.py` | C0 keyword baseline |
| `triage/prompts/base.md`, `triage/prompts/fewshot.md` | C1 prompt, and the C3 prompt with the same text plus the examples |
| `triage/configs.yaml` | C0 to C3 definitions |
| `spe/evals/data/tickets-r01.jsonl` | 60 tickets with no labels. This is the only data file trials can read. |
| `spe/evals/gold/r01-gold.jsonl` | Gold labels, read only by the grader |
| `spe/evals/grader/grade.py`, `spe/evals/grader/selftest.py` | Code checks only. r01 has no LLM judges because every graded field is a label. |
| `spe/evals/control/r01-control.jsonl` | Hand-built outputs with a known joint score of exactly 30 of 60 |
| `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` | The round's Workflow script, with `const ROUND = "r01"` |

### Gates before launch

1. Grader selftest. The oracle (gold as output) must score 100% joint. Empty output must score 0 and fail the schema check. Shifted labels must score at most 15%.
2. Control regrade. No prior round exists, so the control is `r01-control.jsonl`. The grader must score it at exactly 30 of 60.
3. Dry run on 2 cells: C1 and C2 on 3 tickets each. I check the schema, the usage log, the cost math, and that no request payload contains a gold field.

If any gate fails, I halt and report. I will not launch.

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "configs": ["C0", "C1", "C2", "C3"],
  "repeats": 3,
  "dataset": "spe/evals/data/tickets-r01.jsonl",
  "budget_usd": 10,
  "split_extra_max": 2,
  "split_ticket_cap": 20
}
```

The script holds `ROUND` itself. No prompt text contains a typed round number.

### Workflow phases

1. Trials. One agent runs each config and repeat cell (10 cells). Each agent runs `triage/agent.py` and returns a schema with `config`, `repeat`, `outputs_path`, `calls`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, and `cost_usd`. Workflow agents use Opus.
2. Budget guard. Before each cell, the script projects spend from the dry-run cost per call. It skips any cell that would cross $10 and logs the skip to `spe/evals/results/r01/skips.md`.
3. Peek scan. The script scans each trial transcript for reads of `spe/evals/gold/`, `spe/evals/grader/`, or `spe/predictions/`. It voids any trial that peeked and logs the void. A leaked answer key halts the round.
4. Grade. `grade.py` writes `spe/evals/results/r01/scores.json` with code checks only.
5. Split cells. A ticket splits when its 3 repeats disagree on `joint_ok`. Each split ticket gets up to 2 extra runs, for at most 20 tickets per config.
6. Failure analysis. One agent reads the wrong outputs next to gold and groups them into F-numbered types.
7. Completeness critic. One agent checks that every predicted cell has a measured number, and that every skip, void, and split is explained.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

- API spend for trials is about $1.60 for the base runs plus up to $0.50 for split reruns, so about $2 in total under the $10 cap. This is an estimate.
- Workflow agent usage is about 12 Opus agent runs. This is an estimate and has not been measured.
- Wall time is about 30 to 60 minutes. This is an estimate.

Do not edit after the run.`, with author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs, numbers, a Why per number, and `same_as_last_round: null` because this is the first round. | `SPE r01 predict: no config meets both bars, C1 cheap, C2 and C3 accurate` |
| 3 | Build the agent, dataset, gold, grader, control, and workflow. Run the 3 gates and save their output. | `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): agent C0 to C3, 60 tickets, grader, gates passed` |

Add a "Proposed for round 2" table to the spec. Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`. Update `spe/README.md`. | `SPE r01 learn: <prediction accuracy summary>`, then tag `spe-r01` |

I will never edit `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` after a trial runs. A grader bug found after the run goes into `failures.md`, with the original and regraded numbers side by side.

## 5. Halt conditions

I stop and report to you if any of these happen:

- The spend would cross the $10 cap.
- A trial reads gold, graders, or predictions.
- A gate fails, or a grader bug changes a verdict.
- A choice comes up that only you can make, such as switching to real ticket data.

I will not push, deploy, or send anything.
critiques: The answer quotes the prompt as the spec. Its Requirements table maps "correctly" and "cheaply" to R2 and R4 through logged defaults D3 and D4. Each of R1 to R8 has a Test column entry such as `joint_ok`, `cost_per_1k`, or `inject_hold`.

The Predicted numbers table gives C0 to C3 concrete values for every metric. Examples are joint accuracy 45/83/90/87 and cost 0.00/1.50/4.50/3.10 USD per 1,000 tickets. No cell uses an adjective in place of a number.

Every metric row has a Why column that explains its numbers. The joint row breaks C1's score down by ticket group, and the cost row gives the token and price arithmetic. The Why is written once per row, not once per cell, but it covers each config's value.

Step 2 copies the plan to `spe/plans/r01.md` and writes `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` with a do-not-edit header. It commits both as "SPE r01 predict". This happens before step 3 builds the harness and before step 4 launches the Workflow.

The eval is a Workflow script (`r01-workflow.js`). The "Gates before launch" section requires a grader selftest (oracle, empty output, and shifted labels) and a control regrade. It also requires a 2-cell dry run on 3 tickets each, and the plan halts if any gate fails.

Each metric row names its grader check in the first column, for example `cat_exact`, `team_exact`, `pri_exact`, `joint_ok`, `p1_recall`, `inject_hold`, `schema_ok`, and `cost_per_1k`. The "All bars met" row is derived from those checks.

Step 6 writes `spe/prediction-log.md` with Predicted, Measured, Verdict, and "Which Why broke" sections. It also adds a "Proposed for round 2" table and writes `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml`, which seeds the next round.
